audit_findings.title: Post-close Dellner financing breaks the valuation perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,053 million acquisition; debt increased $1,030 million from $5,541 million at 2025-12-31 to $6,571 million at 2026-06-30; first-half interest expense increased $59 million year over year; net value effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The pre-Dellner OE anchor is projected against a post-close cash and capital structure while debt principal is not deducted, so Dellner earnings and the full recurring after-tax financing cost must instead enter forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The transaction subsequently closed on February 10, 2026, and was funded with a combination of cash on hand and borrowings under other sources of available liquidity.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Omitting Dellner earnings understates value, while omitting its financing cost overstates value. Acquisitions contributed $457 million of first-half 2026 sales, including $110 million from Dellner, but the filings do not isolate their OE contribution. The size of the transaction, debt increase and interest increase makes the unresolved net effect reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios from a same-perimeter pro forma or trailing-twelve-month OE base that includes Dellner, full-period Inspection Technologies and Frauscher results, acquisition accounting effects, cash used and after-tax interest on post-anchor borrowings.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-funded growth may be valued without its required capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,494 million of 2025 net acquisition cash, equal to 177.7% of the $1,403.8 million OE anchor; acquisitions supplied $355 million of 2025 sales growth versus $464 million of organic sales growth
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth enters the OE projection, but acquisition purchase spending and any incremental financing needed to produce that growth are outside the modeled equity cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, Wabtec acquired Inspection Technologies for net cash of approximately $(1,729) million and Frauscher for net cash of approximately $(765) million.
audit_findings.explanation: It is not demonstrated that the 7% and 9% forecasts require acquisitions, but that dependency is unresolved. The filed acquisition spending is larger than annual anchor OE, and acquisition growth was a substantial portion of 2025 growth. Continued acquisition-supported growth without corresponding investment could therefore materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Calculate same-perimeter organic OE growth excluding acquired results and purchase-accounting effects; rerun any scenario exceeding sustainable organic growth with normalized acquisition investment and after-tax financing costs, or with a lower growth rate.

audit_findings.title: GE holds a subsidiary preferred claim not represented by common shares
audit_findings.magnitude: No preferred claim disclosed at 2026-06-30; the $19 million distribution to/redemption of noncontrolling interest equals 0.075% of the $25,243 million base equity value, or $0.11 per modeled share
audit_findings.mechanism: An outstanding subsidiary preferred claim would require a bridge deduction, preferred distributions in OE, or conversion dilution in shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Each guarantor is 100% owned by the Parent Company, with the exception of GE Transportation, a Wabtec Company, which has 15,000 shares outstanding of Class A Non-Voting Preferred Stock held by General Electric Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 10-K demonstrated that the claim existed, but the latest 10-Q states that every guarantor is 100% parent-owned and reports a $19 million distribution to/redemption of noncontrolling interest. That evidence indicates the preferred interest was extinguished before the valuation date. Even the full $19 million is immaterial relative to modeled base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm from the redemption documentation that the $19 million transaction fully extinguished GE's preferred dividend, liquidation, redemption and conversion rights; no rerun is needed if confirmed.

audit_findings.title: Accrual contract profits may not equal distributable owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes in estimated contract revenue, costs and margins flow through accrual net income and therefore the OE anchor before or after the associated customer cash is received.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the significance of judgments in the estimation process, it is likely that materially different revenue and cost amounts could be recorded if we used different assumptions or if the underlying circumstances were to change.
audit_findings.explanation: The estimation exposure is real and was a critical audit matter, but the record does not demonstrate optimistic recognition or quantify cumulative catch-up effects. Contract assets declined from $720 million to $608 million during 2025 and to $587 million by 2026-06-30, while contract liabilities exceeded contract assets, so the balance-sheet trend alone does not establish overstatement. Materiality remains unresolved because the amount of over-time revenue and historical estimate revisions is not supplied.
audit_findings.action: Obtain over-time revenue, gross-margin catch-up adjustments, estimate-to-actual contract results, contract-asset aging and loss-provision history; rerun the anchor using normalized cash conversion if those data show persistent premature profit recognition.

audit_findings.title: Remaining Integration 3.0 costs are absent from a mechanical growth forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: $37 million to $57 million of estimated restructuring charges remaining at 2026-06-30, computed from the $80 million to $100 million program estimate less $43 million incurred to date; equal to 2.6% to 4.1% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Remaining cash restructuring charges and related implementation capital reduce forecast OE or require explicit investment deductions before projected synergy benefits are credited.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company anticipates that it will incur one-time restructuring charges related to Integration 3.0 of approximately $ 80 million to $ 100 million.
audit_findings.explanation: These are announced future costs rather than a demonstrated error in historical OE. The filed remaining charge range alone is only $0.22 to $0.33 per modeled share before discounting and would not change the broad valuation conclusion, but additional capital investment is unquantified and the forecast should not credit benefits without their costs.
audit_findings.action: Track quarterly cash charges and Integration 3.0 capital expenditures; include their timing in the forecast when management provides an implementation schedule, paired with only the synergies supported by that schedule.

audit_findings.title: Cash-settled RSUs appear to be counted as equity dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: At most 519,322 latest filed restricted shares and units, or 0.30% of the 170.384407 million-share denominator; removing the entire combined balance would increase stated scenario values by no more than approximately $0.50 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash-settled RSUs belong in compensation expense or liabilities, not common-equivalent shares; including them in shares while retaining their expense double-counts the cost.
audit_findings.evidence: The restricted stock units are liability-classified equity awards as they can be settled in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification concern is valid, but the exact cash-settled RSU subset is not disclosed and cannot exceed the 519,322 combined restricted-share-and-unit balance at 2026-06-30. Even treating the entire balance as erroneously included changes the denominator by only 0.30% and cannot materially alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the award-level split between restricted stock, share-settled units and cash-settled RSUs, then rerun per-share values excluding only the cash-settled units while retaining their compensation cost.
